overview: This Senate resolution congratulates Pope Leo XIV on his election as head of the worldwide Catholic Church, noting that he is the first pope ever elected from the United States. It praises his commitment to human dignity, helping the poor, dialogue between faiths, and peace. It expresses hope that ties between the United States and the Holy See, the Vatican's government, will keep growing, and offers best wishes for his time as pope. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on May 22, 2025.
for: Supporters say it marks a historic first for the United States and recognizes the importance of the papacy to more than a billion Catholics worldwide.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or policy; some may also question whether a legislative body should formally congratulate a religious leader.
